subject: Polaris Labs — Replatform economics and rollback protections
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Park <alex.park@polarislabs.ai>, Procurement <procurement@polarislabs.ai>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Polaris Labs — replatform overlay and conditional rollback ask

Alex / team,

Thanks for the time earlier — good conversation on expected monthly QPS and the mixed batch/stream profile. As discussed, I wanted to put a concise proposal on the table for price alignment + a rollback protection mechanism so your finance and platform teams can evaluate risk.

High-level offering:
- Conditional, time-limited price match to your incumbent list price for the first 6 months (applies to committed token volumes; overage billed at standard host rates)
- One-time migration credit bucket: $40k applied against first invoice
- 90-day rollback protection: if Polaris decides to revert to current vendor within 90 days of go-live, we will provide a technical and commercial rollback package covering migration costs up to $20k and a prorated credit on unused committed months
- SLA carveout: 99.5% uptime target with service credits ramping after 5% deviation; rollback trigger tied to repeated P99 latency breaches (details in doc)

Attached: Polaris_Replatform_Overlay.pdf (slide-level econ and timeline). Connor will follow up on the KV-cache/implementation notes.

Next steps: If procurement wants a formal term sheet/DocuSign, we can produce a short addendum that ties the match conditions to a 12-month minimum commitment and a mutual exit window. Happy to jump on a call Thursday.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0124

Subject: Re: Polaris Labs — replatform overlay and conditional rollback ask

Thanks Vanessa — appreciate the clarity.

A couple of clarifying questions from our side before we loop legal:

1) How does the 90-day rollback protection interact with the committed volume credit? If we roll back after 60 days, do you return the $40k credit or offset it against migration costs?
2) The SLA language looks reasonable — can you confirm whether the rollback trigger requires 3 consecutive P99 SLA breaches or a cumulative measurement over the 90-day window?
3) Any required deposit or up-front prepayment to qualify for the matched pricing? Our CFO prefers minimal upfront cash movement.

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Polaris Labs — replatform overlay and conditional rollback ask (internal)

Vanessa / Karthik,

Quick internal note so we can standardize the response to procurement:

Proposed mechanics (we can put in a short addendum):
- Match Condition: Redwood will match incumbent per-unit list price for the first 6 months provided Polaris signs a 12-month term and commits to a minimum monthly token volume (we should propose a 10% buffer above estimated usage).
- Migration credit treatment: the $40k migration credit is non-refundable; if rollback occurs within 90 days, up to $20k of the migration credit can be reallocated to cover documented migration expenses incurred by Polaris (i.e., we don't 'refund' cash — we provide a reconciliation credit on final invoice or a one-off payment if mutually agreed).
- Deposit: No upfront deposit required to qualify. Instead, require a 30-day notice for early cancellation to avoid abuse of the match program.
- SLA/Rollback trigger: rollback commercial remedies are triggered by one of the following: (a) 3 separate days within a 14-day sliding window where P99 latency exceeds agreed threshold by X%, or (b) cumulative P99 degradation exceeding Y% over the 90-day period. Legal will prefer the cumulative metric; ops likes discrete events. Recommend we offer cumulative metric with discrete-events escape hatch.

Ask: Vanessa — can you send back to Polaris with the addendum language and a short DocuSign-ready term sheet? I'll attach the technical appendix (KV cache and warmup runbook) once you have a go/no-go.

Connor
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Park <alex.park@polarislabs.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@polarislabs.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 5 Sep 2026 11:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Polaris Labs — replatform overlay and conditional rollback ask

Alex,

Thanks — appreciate the questions. Below is a compact set of mechanics we can include in the term sheet. I'll attach a short addendum (rollback_terms_draft.docx) for legal; if that looks good we can put the full package into DocuSign.

Term sheet excerpt:
- Price Match: Redwood will match Polaris's incumbent list price for the first six (6) months after go-live, conditioned on a signed 12-month Master Services Agreement and committed minimum monthly token volume (10% buffer recommended).
- Migration Credit: $40,000 one-time migration credit applied to the first invoice. If Polaris elects to rollback within 90 days, up to $20,000 of the migration credit may be used to cover documented rollback expenses; remaining credit is not refundable cash.
- No Upfront Deposit: No prepayment or deposit is required to qualify for the match. Standard billing terms (net-30) apply.
- Rollback Trigger and Remedies: Commercial rollback remedies are available if Redwood misses the agreed P99 latency threshold under either:
   • a cumulative P99 degradation of >15% measured over the 90-day post-go-live window; OR
   • three (3) separate days within any 14-day sliding window where P99 latency exceeds the threshold by >25%.
  If triggered, Redwood will (a) provide a migration-cost reimbursement up to $20k, (b) issue a prorated credit for unused committed months, and (c) offer an ops-runbook to assist with rollback.
- SLA and Credits: Target uptime 99.5%; service credits begin after the first full month with measured deviation beyond SLA. Details in attached addendum.

If this meets procurement's expectations we can circulate a DocuSign addendum by EOD Tuesday. Happy to jump on a brief call with Dominic to walk through the rollback mechanics.

Best regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
